input.rationale: The only inbound grant to us is Section 1.4 (p0008-p0009): HDI provides "the Company" with access to, and the right to use, HDI's computer system, software and Content administration tools. That right runs to the Company alone — "affiliate" and "contractor" appear nowhere in the Agreement — and Section 10.3 closes the door entirely ("no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement"), so affiliates are excluded with no path to add them. That fails fallback element 1 and edges into walk-away territory, so a redline is warranted. Fallback element 2 is already met: Section 10.3 makes the Agreement (and therefore the Section 1.4 use rights) binding on and enforceable by the parties' legal representatives, successors and assigns, which covers a successor by merger or acquisition. We therefore target the fallback with the shortest possible change — one sentence extending the Section 1.4 access and use rights to affiliates identified by written notice. Preferred-position sub-elements (contractors acting on our behalf, perpetual/irrevocable paid-up rights, termination only for uncured material breach) are noted but not pursued, as this is a term hosting arrangement with no paid-up or subscription licence; they are not treated as separate deviations. The trademark licence in Section 6.1 is outbound (we license our "Deerskin" Marks to HDI) and is not flagged under this rule.

proposal.summary: Extend the Section 1.4 access and use rights to Company affiliates identified by written notice.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our licence position requires affiliate coverage, so we have added that the Section 1.4 access and use rights extend to any Company affiliate identified to HDI by written notice; Section 10.3 already carries those rights to our successors and assigns.

ops.text: The access and right to use granted to the Company under this Section 1.4 shall extend to any affiliate of the Company identified to HDI by written notice.
